messages:
vuln-bot: New NVD entry detected: CVE-2026-0001 affecting `httpx` <=0.25.1. RCE via malformed header parsing. CVSS: 9.1, EPSS: 0.75. PoC referenced: https://github.com/advisories/CVE-2026-0001 :eyes:

amanda: ugh. which services use httpx in prod? any public exploit verified? :thinking:

ben: quick scan of the infra images: `grype` run earlier flagged 8 images with vulnerable httpx versions out of 42 scanned (see link). PoC repo shows header vector that matches our ingress parsing patterns. link: https://internal/scans/1954321

chandra: EPSS high + PoC public => treat P1 until mitigated. impact: potential remote code execution from unauthenticated requests. We should assume exploitability until proven otherwise.

leo: listing owners: `serving-runtime` uses httpx in the Python worker, `batch-ingest` uses it for webhooks, and `tooling/cli` bundles a pinned httpx. I'll open PRs to bump to 0.26.1 and add header-length checks. will canary 5% first.

marc: oncall plan: 1) block crafted header pattern at edge WAF rule, 2) deploy patched worker to canary, 3) monitor errors and latency. rollback plan: route traffic back to previous revision and remove WAF rule if false positive.

amanda: do we need KMS / secrets rotation? could exploit read KMS credentials?

chandra: KMS not directly affected. Attack surface is request handling and arbitrary code execution in process. If any endpoint returns credentials or signs tokens, consider rotating keys as a precaution for affected services only. For Dedicated/Private customers, flag for manual outreach.

ben: quick grep to find occurrences:```
# find httpx deps
rg "httpx" --hidden --glob '!node_modules' -S || true
# check runtime package list in images
docker run --rm myimage:tag pip show httpx || true
```

devops-bot: Container scan summary: 8 vulnerable images (serving-runtime:3, batch-ingest:2, tooling/cli:1, experiments:2). Auto-ticket created: SEC-3487.

oncall: any chance this affects the hosted inference API proxy (edge)? we must avoid customer-facing outage.

leo: edge proxies use `uvicorn` + `httpx` for a few healthcheck/forwarding tasks. I'll exclude edge from immediate change — instead apply WAF rule at the edge to reject suspicious header shapes, then patch backend workers. Canary plan to avoid breaking customers.

chandra: scoring notes for tracker: CVSS 9.1 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), EPSS 0.75, public PoC => exploitability: high. Recommend urgency: P1, SLO: patch to 0.26.1 within 24h for prod; mitigations (WAF + input sanitization) within 6h.

amanda: action items: @leo open PRs to bump and add header guard (assign to @marc for rollout), @ben run full image rebuilds for vulnerable images and attach SBOMs, @chandra notify Customer Success for Dedicated customers. Can we get quick ETA?

leo: PRs created: https://git.internal/serving-runtime/pulls/432 (bump), https://git.internal/batch-ingest/pulls/78 (bump + header check). planning canary deploy in ~30m.

marc: will own rollout and observability. I'll add tracing flags, enable increased sampling for errors, and set up an alert for suspicious `header` parse exceptions.

devops-bot: CI builds triggered for PRs: #432, #78. Continuous scans requeued.

ben: putting temporary mitigation checklist in the ticket: 1) WAF rule deny header regex 2) rate-limit suspicious user agents 3) deploy patched images to canary 4) verify logs for exploit attempts 5) backport to older minor releases if needed.

amanda: thanks all. please update SEC-3487 with status. if anything changes (exploit matured), we escalate to incident channel. :thumbsup:

chandra: quick KMS note for the tracker: if any service uses instance-level KMS ACLs, include the KMS resource ARNs in SEC-3487 so we can advise rotation scope.

leo: noted, adding ARNs to the ticket now.

marc: post-deploy quickscore: initial canary shows no errors after 45m, telemetry normal. will push to 20% after 2h if stable.

oncall: thanks team, leaving monitor on overnight.

vuln-bot: closing advisory update: NVD will push patch note; will ping thread if new PoC emerges.
